Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at our host institution is straightforward and user-friendly. It begins with an online application where you provide your personal and academic information. Once your application is reviewed and accepted, you will receive an email with further instructions. This includes setting up your student portal, where you can register for courses, pay fees, and access important resources. Support staff are always available to assist you throughout the process, ensuring a smooth and stress-free experience.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At our host institution, a variety of help is available to support students. Academic advisors are on hand to assist with course selection and academic planning. There are also tutoring services for additional academic support. For personal and emotional well-being, counseling services are readily accessible. The IT helpdesk provides technical assistance for any issues related to online platforms or devices. Additionally, there are numerous workshops and seminars aimed at skill development and career planning. The institution ensures comprehensive support to help you succeed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful in registering for the classes I wanted. The registration system is efficient, and I found it easy to navigate. Most of the classes I aimed for had available spots, and the few that were full had clear waitlist options. The academic advisors were very helpful in suggesting alternative courses that fit well with my schedule and academic goals. Overall, I was able to secure a schedule that I’m very happy with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For future exchange students, my advice would be to start the registration process early. This ensures you have the best chance of getting into your preferred classes. Utilize the resources available, such as academic advisors, who can guide you in selecting the right courses. Be flexible and have a few backup options in mind, as some classes may fill up quickly. Finally, familiarize yourself with the online registration system ahead of time to make the process smoother. Being proactive and prepared will make your registration experience much more successful and stress-free.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses at our host institution varies widely, accommodating different academic needs and backgrounds. There are introductory courses that provide a solid foundation for beginners, often with a focus on fundamental concepts and skills. Intermediate courses build on this foundation, offering more in-depth exploration of subjects and requiring some prior knowledge. Advanced courses are available for those who have a strong background in the subject, offering specialized and comprehensive study, often with a focus on critical thinking, research, and practical application. Regardless of the level, the courses are designed to be engaging, challenging, and supportive, ensuring that all students can achieve their academic goals.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at my host institution has some distinct differences compared to the University of Copenhagen (UCPH). At the host institution, there is a strong emphasis on interactive and participatory learning. Classes often involve discussions, group work, and hands-on activities, which help to engage students actively in the learning process. In contrast, UCPH tends to have a more lecture-based approach, though it also incorporates interactive elements. The host institution also offers a variety of online resources and platforms to complement in-person teaching, providing a more blended learning experience. Overall, both institutions strive to deliver high-quality education, but the host institution leans more towards an interactive, student-centered teaching style.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
During my exchange, I noticed some items were more or less expensive than expected:

More Expensive:

Groceries and Dining Out: The cost of food, both in stores and restaurants, was higher than I had budgeted for.
Transportation: Public transport and occasional taxi rides added up more quickly than expected.
Personal Care Items: Toiletries and other personal care products were more expensive than I was used to.
Less Expensive:

Clothing: I found that clothing, especially during sales, was more affordable than I expected.
Entertainment: Local events, student discounts for cultural attractions, and cinema tickets were reasonably priced.
Utilities: If you live off-campus, utility costs were quite manageable compared to other living expenses.
Overall, balancing these costs and taking advantage of student discounts helped manage my budget effectively.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
At my host institution, there was a vibrant array of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students:

Cultural Activities:

Cultural Nights and Festivals: Regular events celebrating various cultures through music, dance, and food.
Language Exchange Programs: Opportunities to practice languages with native speakers and international students.
Museum Visits and Art Exhibitions: Organized trips to local museums and galleries.
Athletic Activities:

Intramural Sports: Opportunities to join recreational sports leagues and tournaments.
Fitness Classes: Regular classes such as yoga, pilates, and martial arts.
Gym Facilities: Access to well-equipped gyms and fitness centers on campus.
Social Activities:

Student Clubs and Organizations: A wide range of clubs covering interests from academic subjects to hobbies and cultural groups.
Orientation and Welcome Events: Activities to help new students integrate and make friends.
Social Mixers and Parties: Organized social events like barbecues, parties, and themed nights.
These activities not only enriched the cultural experience but also provided opportunities to meet new people and create lasting memories during the exchange period.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There was a rich variety of cultural events, diverse athletic opportunities, and vibrant social activities available for students at my host institution.




I recommend visiting students explore local landmarks, try regional cuisine, and participate in cultural festivals during weekends or holidays. It's a great way to immerse yourself in the local culture and make memorable experiences. Graveensten is a good example

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting students explore the historic city center of Ghent, including Gravensteen Castle and St. Bavo's Cathedral. Take a boat tour along the canals, enjoy Belgian waffles and chocolates, and visit local museums like the Design Museum Gent. Additionally, exploring the lively Korenmarkt square and nearby parks like Citadel Park can offer relaxing and enjoyable experiences during weekends or holidays in Ghent.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture of my exchange site was surprisingly easy. The people were welcoming, and there were many cultural activities and resources available to help me integrate smoothly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Attend Social Events: Participate in student clubs, cultural nights, or sports events where you can meet new people.

Learn the Language: Even basic phrases in the local language can go a long way in connecting with locals and showing respect for their culture.

Join Study Groups: Collaborating on coursework can naturally lead to friendships and deeper connections with local students.

Explore Shared Interests: Whether it's music, sports, or hobbies, find common interests that can serve as conversation starters.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The transition from Denmark to Belgium posed challenges in adjusting to a more relaxed and less structured approach to daily life, which was different from the organized and efficient Danish culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I most appreciated the emphasis on work-life balance, the strong sense of community, and the appreciation for art and history in the local culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Embrace the local culture: Enjoy Ghent's historical charm and vibrant cultural scene. Attend festivals, explore local cuisine, and interact with locals to fully immerse yourself.

Get involved: Join student clubs, attend events, and participate in activities to meet new people and make the most of your exchange experience.

Plan your travels: Take advantage of Ghent's central location to explore other parts of Belgium and nearby European cities during weekends and holidays.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Consider exploring nearby cities like Bruges and Brussels for day trips. They offer unique cultural experiences and are easily accessible by train from Ghent.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was forming friendships with people from different cultures and backgrounds, creating lasting connections and memories that enriched my worldview.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was navigating the initial cultural differences and adjusting to a new academic environment and daily routine.
